lines: Welcome to the library. Quiet, please.
Crane and Inkwell will duel you first. Then, if you like, me.
Patience folds every crane.
In my club, I begin every round holding Reverse. Be careful what you win.
A fine fold. I bow to you.
The Paper stamp is yours. Oh… something slipped out of my sleeve. Never mind it.

win.goal: A folded note fell by the shelves in the library. Read it.

lines: Patience wins again. Watch what I never do.
Crane and Inkwell first, please. Patience.
A folded note, stamped STUDENT COUNCIL.
"Proposal: replace Hand Duels with a fair lottery, starting at the school festival. Clubs to be closed. — R."
(The Council wants to ban duels?! The Fencing Club will want to hear about this.)

memo.goal: Show the memo to the Fencing Club in the sports hall.

lines: A memo? From the Council?! A BAN?
Then we duel twice as hard. Parry! Riposte! Test this one!
You got past my two best. Good.
In my hall we fight speed rounds: the countdown is faster. Keep up!
Touché! I'll remember that one.
The Blade stamp is yours. The whole school's splitting over this ban. Watch your back.
En garde next time! And watch what I do after I lose.
Parry and Riposte first! Then me!
Like the new look? I've joined the Student Council.
A lottery means nobody ever has to lose again. Isn't that better?
Then prove it.
"Maybe" isn't good enough. Duel me and decide.
…That's exactly why I hate losing.
See? Wouldn't you rather this was a lottery?
At the festival, the lottery wins. You'll see.

rio_ch3.goal: The Drama Club is rehearsing in the auditorium (corridor, fourth door).
